declarations.notes: The notation table is encoded with natural-number indices, explicit real-to-complex coordinates, and the complex norm form of |q| < 1.
The source says δ is arbitrary small and positive; the declaration states the precise existence property used by later estimates.

Gamma and psi use the canonical complex Mathlib objects. betaFunction is Mathlib's Euler interval integral, whose convergence theorem uses 0 < Re a and 0 < Re b; it is not the meromorphic continuation. q-Gamma remains defined in Section518.
Historical Pi/Psi/F notation is represented by shifted aliases of the canonical Gamma and digamma objects.
Nat specialization of the source's general-complex factorial alternative: z = n + 1 and ordinary n.factorial.
Euler's constant is Mathlib's Real.eulerMascheroniConstant. A prime is exposed as Mathlib's totalized complex deriv and is intended only where differentiability has been established.

shared_vocabulary_requests: Keep Section518.qGamma as the single q-Gamma implementation; if a chapter-wide notation namespace is introduced later, re-export it there rather than duplicating it in Section51.
known_gaps: DLMF §5.1 has no numbered equations; all coverage is recorded as notation and convention anchors.
The source's prose does not define a separate Lean object for 'real or complex variable'; the formalization uses ℂ with canonical coercions and explains that choice in the manual.
